title: Mnemonic Similarity Task: A Tool for Assessing Hippocampal Integrity
authors: Shauna M. Stark, C. Brock Kirwan, Craig E. L. Stark
caption_short: Panel A shows the MST trial sequence - an incidental encoding phase with indoor/outdoor judgements followed by a test phase in which exact repetitions, similar lures and novel foils each require an 'old' / 'similar' / 'new' response - and panel B shows example encoding/test image pairs for the five lure-similarity bins.
license: author manuscript, PMC (NIHMS-1545640); published version copyright Elsevier - figure reproduced under fair use for academic summary
notes: The PMCID given in the request (PMC6825892) is wrong - it resolves to an unrelated Gynecologic Oncology article. The correct record for this paper is PMID 31597601 / PMC6991464, confirmed via PubMed esummary and EuropePMC. Figure 1 in the author manuscript sits on p. 23 of the 24-page PDF (figures are collected at the end). The PNG was extracted at native resolution (958x1050, 150 dpi) from the figure's embedded JPEG object rather than from a page raster - pdfimages confirms the PDF's page-23 image is exactly this asset (nihms-1545640-f0001.jpg), so no resampling was applied; only the uniform white border was trimmed. Panel A is the paradigm proper; panel B was kept because the lure-similarity bins are the graded manipulation the MST is built around. Colored boxes in panel A are the authors' annotation and are not shown to participants. An author-deposited CC-BY copy also exists at eScholarship (https://escholarship.org/uc/item/3h17g413) but its CDN refused all automated requests; the PMC author manuscript was used instead.
